question: What claim about the kinds of linguistic forms encountered is being made by distinguishing heard and unheard languages of varied form?
premises: Languages of varied form are present as a distinct class.
Some of those forms fall into the class of what has been heard.
Some of those forms fall into the class of what has not been heard.
inference: The field of languages includes both heard and unheard forms of varied appearance.
uncertainties: It is not specified here whether the distinction is perceptual or ontological.
plain_english: Languages of varied form indeed appear, both heard and unheard, and so on in that distinction.
